title.narrative: Making Lebanese Decision-Makers More Responsive to Citizens’ Needs

description.narrative:
This two-year project aims to strengthen the responsiveness of Lebanese decision-makers to citizens' priorities by building bridges between public opinion and decision makers. Led by the Lebanese Center for Policy Studies (LCPS), the initiative will collect and analyze nationwide public perception data, engage stakeholders through structured dialogues, and produce accessible, evidence-based policy outputs. By empowering reform-minded actors with reliable insights and securing inclusive forums for exchange, the project will contribute to more transparent, accountable, and citizen-driven governance during a critical moment of political transition and institutional recovery in Lebanon.
IMPACT: Restore trust between citizens and decision-makers in Lebanon by supporting participatory, evidence-based reforms aligned with public needs and monitoring government progress.
OUTCOME 1: Understanding Public Perception OUTPUT 1.1: In-person survey (CAPI) executed across all governorates. OUTPUT 1.2: 36 FGDs conducted with diverse demographics to contextualize survey. OUTPUT 1.3: Survey and FGD data translated into visuals
OUTCOME 2: Stakeholder-informed policy reforms developed and refined through structured dialogue. OUTPUT 2.1: Multi-stakeholder discussions foster consensus on reform. OUTPUT 2.2: Decision-makers and experts provide insights to guide policy briefs.
OUTCOME 3 Citizens and CSOs equipped to monitor reform progress and hold decision-makers accountable. OUTPUT 3.1: Bi-monthly monitors report on reform progress and hold decision-makers accountable. OUTPUT 3.2: Translate complex policy issues into digestible, engaging content for broad audiences.
OUTCOME 4: wider dissemination of results OUTPUT 4.1 Key MPs and advisors briefed in closed sessions. OUTPUT 4.Public Dissemination of outputs.
Target groups: Policymakers, elected officials, civil servants, youth and women, civil society organizations, media, and citizens across Lebanon
